text:
maya: quick sync — acme enterprise asked for a per-tenant canary that can escalate automatically to their reserved capacity if latency or error-rate crosses a threshold. they want the ability to set the thresholds from the console and an emergency cutoff.

jordan: sounds reasonable. need to confirm Product constraints: how much control do we give the tenant vs ops? can they flip failover on?

maya: they should be able to request a canary window and thresholds via API/console, but ops retains the final escalation permission. user flips go into a pending state that requires ops approval for first-time escalations. after that we can autonotify.

sam: engineering question — do we implement this as a traffic-split + health-checker or as a shadow divert with live promotion? traffic-split will exercise the runtime. if we want safe isolation for dedicated tenants we should avoid shared KV cache for the canary slice.

priya: from SRE perspective we need automated abort based on metrics and a cooldown. propose: abort if p95 > 800ms OR error_rate > 3% for 2m rolling. then a 10m cooldown and failover to reserved. also add token-cost spike guard (>2x baseline) to prevent runaway charges.

sam: agreed. suggest these defaults but make them editable per-tenant. technical sketch for policy payload:```json
{
  "policy": "per-tenant-canary",
  "traffic_split": {"canary": 0.05, "stable": 0.95},
  "abort_on": {"p95_latency_ms": ">800", "error_rate_percent": ">3", "token_cost_multiplier": ">2"},
  "cooldown_minutes": 10,
  "failover_action": "route-to-dedicated-pool"
}
```

jordan: console UX: slider for traffic split, toggles for abort_on rules (preset: conservative / balanced / aggressive), preview of expected cost delta, and a big red “escalate now” button for ops.

maya: we also need audit logging + trace linking: every canary decision should emit an event to audit and create a trace id that ties into console timeline.

priya: telemetry: must show p50/p95/p99, error_rate, 1m,5m rolling windows, and the request distribution by model variant. plus a one-click download of the canary request sample for manual QA.

sam: implementation notes — runtime needs to support per-tenant routing rule that pins a subset of connections to the canary variant without cross-tenant prefix cache. that means a per-tenant cache key namespace for the slice. fallback routing should be deterministic so we can reason about warmed KV caches.

maya: perf concern: spinning up dedicated GPUs for failover is slow. ops wants a warm standby (0-1 instance warm) — how do we account for cost? maybe a reserved warm pool charging model.

jordan: product okay with warm-standby as an add-on for enterprise. pricing/contract to handle it.

priya: edge case: what if canary causes downstream quota exhaustion (upstream DB or token quota)? plan to detect dependent quotas and abort early; add a dependent_quota flag in policy to monitor.

sam: API change: POST /rollouts -> {rollout_policy}, PATCH /rollouts/:id/traffic to adjust split, POST /rollouts/:id/escalate for ops. need API schema and migration.

maya: +1. can we also add a server-side dry-run mode so we can simulate the canary decision engine on historical telemetry? that’ll help sales/admins approve thresholds.

sam: we can run a replay job that re-simulates rules over a metrics window. will add a job in infra.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary-controller:feature/per-tenant-failsafe queued for staging (sha: a1b2c3).

jordan: action items — sam: design API + runtime changes, priya: SLO rules and telemetry contract, maya: console mockups and audit requirements. I'll own product PR and docs. aim for staging deploy end of next week. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — ping me if anything needs product sign-off.

sam: filing RFC + PR link in #eng-platform when ready.
